`tidytmle` brings cross-fitted Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (CV-TMLE) into the `tidymodels` ecosystem as a semi-parametric causal orchestrator sitting above `workflows`, `workflowsets`, `recipes`, `rsample`, `hardhat`, and `yardstick`.

## Level 1: The 3-Line Safe Default

At Level 1, pass `outcome`, `treatment`, `covariates` (via `tidyselect`), and one or more causal `estimand`s to `tmle_spec()`, then call `fit()`. Ten-fold cross-fitting, an ensemble Super Learner library (`glm`, `glmnet`, `ranger`), adaptive positivity bounds, and bounded canonical logistic fluctuation are enabled automatically:

```{r level1, message = FALSE}
library(tidytmle)

cohort <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 350, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 42)
truth <- attr(cohort, "truth")

fit <- tmle_spec(
  outcome    = y,
  treatment  = a,
  covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),
  estimand   = c("ate", "rr", "or")
) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>
  fit(data = cohort)

fit
```

## Joint EIF Inference & Tidymodels S3 Verbs

Standard `tidymodels` S3 verbs extract every layer of the fitted pipeline without digging through nested lists:

```{r verbs}
# Causal inference table with optional simultaneous uniform bands and E-values
tidy(fit, simultaneous = TRUE, e_value = TRUE)

# One-row causal health check
glance(fit)

# Cross-validated nuisance metrics (yardstick) and Super Learner weights
collect_metrics(fit)
extract_sl_weights(fit)
```

Observation-level counterfactual predictions (`.q0_init`, `.q1_init`, `.q0_star`, `.q1_star`), truncated propensity scores (`.g_trunc`), clever covariates (`.clever_h`), and Efficient Influence Function leverage (`.eif_leverage`) are returned by `augment()`:

```{r augment}
head(augment(fit)[, c("age", "a", "y", ".q0_star", ".q1_star", ".g_trunc", ".eif_leverage")])
```

## Instant `retarget()` Without ML Refitting

Because cross-fitted out-of-fold nuisance predictions ($Q_n^0$, $g_n$, $C_n$) are cached inside the `tmle_fit` object, you can test stricter positivity bounds, switch estimands (`"att"`, `"atc"`), or target subgroups in milliseconds without refitting any machine learning models:

```{r retarget}
fit_strict <- retarget(fit, g_bounds = c(0.05, 0.95))
fit_att    <- retarget(fit, estimand = "att")
fit_older  <- retarget(fit, subgroup = age >= 55)

dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit), scenario = "Adaptive bounds (All)"),
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_strict), scenario = "Strict bounds [0.05, 0.95]"),
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_att), scenario = "ATT"),
  dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_older), scenario = "Subgroup age >= 55")
) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, estimand, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)
```

## Visual Causal Diagnostics (`autoplot()`)

Inspect propensity overlap, nuisance learner weights, EIF leverage outliers, positivity sensitivity curves, and weighted covariate balance using `autoplot()`:

```{r plots, fig.alt = "Propensity score overlap and positivity sensitivity sweep"}
autoplot(fit, type = "overlap")
autoplot(fit, type = "sensitivity", g_grid = seq(0.01, 0.12, by = 0.02))
```
